holidays.name: National Macaroon Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the sweet, chewy coconut cookie known as the macaroon. Bakers and snackers alike dig into piles of coconut goodness, and some people confuse it with its fancier French cousin, the macaron.
holidays.origin: A food observance in the United States, popularized by food-holiday calendars. Macaroons trace back to Italian monasteries in the Middle Ages, and the almond-based version spread across Europe before coconut became the star in American recipes.
holidays.funFact: The word macaroon comes from the Italian 'maccarone,' meaning paste, which is the same root as the word macaroni.

holidays.name: World No Tobacco Day
holidays.description: A global awareness day encouraging people to give up tobacco for 24 hours and highlighting the health risks of tobacco use. Campaigns each year pick a different theme, from protecting youth to supporting food growers.
holidays.origin: Established by the World Health Organization's member states in 1987 to draw attention to the tobacco epidemic and its preventable death and disease.
holidays.funFact: Each year the WHO gives World No Tobacco Day Awards to individuals and organizations around the world for their efforts to fight tobacco use.

holidays.name: Save Your Hearing Day
holidays.description: A day for reminding everyone to turn down the volume, protect their ears, and think twice before blasting headphones at full volume. It is a good excuse to give your eardrums a quiet break.
holidays.origin: An awareness observance in the United States, promoted by hearing health advocates to encourage hearing protection and regular hearing checkups.
holidays.funFact: Hearing damage can begin with prolonged exposure to sounds above about 85 decibels, which is roughly the noise level of heavy city traffic.

holidays.name: Brisk Walking Day
holidays.description: A day for lacing up your sneakers and picking up the pace on a brisk walk. It is perfect for people who want exercise without the commitment of running or the sweat of a gym.
holidays.origin: An informal fitness observance promoted by health and wellness communities to encourage moderate daily exercise that is easy on the joints.
holidays.funFact: A brisk walk is generally defined as about 3 to 4 miles per hour, fast enough to raise your heart rate but still let you hold a conversation.

holidays.name: Hug Your Cat Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to showering your feline overlord with affection, assuming the cat consents. Cat owners are encouraged to cuddle, but wise ones accept that the cat sets the terms of any hug.
holidays.origin: A pet-themed unofficial observance created by cat lovers and shared widely online, in keeping with the internet's lasting devotion to cats.
holidays.funFact: Cats can purr at frequencies between 25 and 150 Hertz, a range some researchers think may help promote bone healing.
